ex.9: Δlong = distance / cos lat = 350 / cos 45° ≈ 495' = 8° 15'. A is west of B: 45° 15' − 8° 15' = 37° 00' E.
ex.10: Δlong = departure / cos lat = 1200 / 0.5 = 2400' = 40°, so 100° E + 40° = 140° E.
ex.11: Equal journey time means GS is in proportion to the length of the parallel: 340 / cos 50° ≈ 529 kt.
ex.16: In the southern hemisphere the compass turning errors are reversed: turning through north the compass lags, so roll out after the heading — about 055° for a turn to NE.
ex.20: ATIS winds are magnetic. Angle between wind 210° and runway 047° = 163°, so tailwind = V × cos 17° ≈ 0.956 V. 10 / 0.956 ≈ 10.5 → about 11 kt.
ex.21: QNH is 14 hPa below 1013; at about 27–30 ft/hPa pressure altitude ≈ 25 000 + 400 = 25 400 ft.
ex.28: On a 3° slope ROD ≈ 5 × GS, so 12 kt less GS → about 60 ft/min less.
ex.33: ZFM = TOM − usable fuel = 141 000 − (63 000 − 1000) = 79 000 kg (unusable fuel stays in the ZFM).

ex.41: Book key prints (b). TH = TT − drift right = 180 − 8 = 172°. MH = CH + deviation = 195 − 2 = 193°. Variation = TH − MH = −21°, i.e. 21° W, so the correct answer is (a).
